text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today to $140.52, pulling back from a peak of $142.28 just three days earlier. The stock is giving back gains in a broader energy pullback—oil prices have drifted slightly lower (US crude at $89.62/barrel), and the two-week chart shows the stock up only 4.5% from its November 9th low, suggesting momentum has stalled. No specific company news today explains the decline; the move appears to be a modest profit-taking moment after a sharp four-day rally.

The backdrop remains mixed for refiners and producers. Heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year, which could lift winter demand for refined products, but broader economic uncertainty—rising shipping costs and cautious retail inventory planning—may be tempering near-term sentiment on energy demand more generally.
